type:
∀ {ι κ : Type*} (X : ι → Set Nat) (Y : κ → Set Nat),
  (∀ i, Set.Nonempty (X i)) → (∀ j, Set.Nonempty (Y j)) →
  Pairwise (fun i i' => Disjoint (X i) (X i')) →
  Pairwise (fun j j' => Disjoint (Y j) (Y j')) →
  let U := Subgroup.closure {σ : Equiv.Perm Nat | Equiv.Perm.IsSwap σ}
  let blockSym := fun B : Set Nat => _root_.fixingSubgroup (↥U) Bᶜ
  let H := iSup (fun i => blockSym (X i))
  let G := iSup (fun j => blockSym (Y j))
  ∀ (α β : ↥U)
      (hα : ∀ h : H, α * (h : ↥U) * α⁻¹ ∈ G)
      (hβ : ∀ h : H, β * (h : ↥U) * β⁻¹ ∈ G),
    let a := MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator α hα
    let b := MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator β hβ
    let inBlock := fun (σ : ↥U) (i : ι) (j : κ) =>
      Set.MapsTo (⇑(σ : Equiv.Perm Nat)) (X i) (Y j)
    (∀ i, Set.Nontrivial (X i) →
      (∃ j, inBlock α i j) ∧ (∃ j, inBlock β i j)) ∧
    (Nonempty (MackeyDiagrams.Dot a b) ↔
      ∀ i, Set.Nontrivial (X i) → ∃ j, inBlock α i j ∧ inBlock β i j)
sourceReason: Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 3.4, “A criterion for group-element dots,” p. 11. The published PDF matched the project copy byte for byte, and the project TeX and article HTML agree on the endpoint. The supplied defect-report URL returned HTTP 404 with and without a trailing slash. The task context supplies no corrected statement. The swap closure models the finitary symmetric group on Nat. Each block factor fixes its complement pointwise, and the subgroup supremum represents the product of the disjoint factors inside that finitary group. The block families and blocks may be infinite. The type includes the containment assertion for both embeddings and uses MackeyDiagrams.Dot for existence of a group-element dot. https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects
